items.title: Energy stocks rally as fresh U.S.-Iran attacks drive oil prices higher
items.summary: Investing.com -- U.S.-listed energy stocks climbed in premarket trading Monday, tracking a more than 2% jump in oil prices after American forces struck an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz and Tehran retaliated.

items.title: Chevron vs. Occidental: Which Oil Major's Dividend Is Actually Safer?
items.summary: If you look at the traditional measure of dividend safety, the payout ratio, you may get the wrong impression.

items.title: The Number ExxonMobil No Longer Puts In Front Of Its Results
items.summary: Management's own scorecard still leads with dollars, but the return measure that used to sit beside it was absent again, and that changes what a holder is actually betting on.

items.title: ExxonMobil Stock's Biggest Risk Is The Shortage Ending
items.summary: ExxonMobil's refining and chemical margins rest on capacity that is offline elsewhere, which makes a return to normal supply the risk worth weighing.

items.title: Which Oil and Gas Stock Has Dominated in 2026: ConocoPhillips, EOG Resources, or Occidental Petroleum?
items.summary: Three oil and gas giants have chased each other so closely through 2026 that the real winner might surprise you, and it is not the one most investors expected to pull ahead.

items.title: Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.A) Holds Firm As A Top Portfolio Stake Lifts Its Dividend
items.summary: Occidental Petroleum (NYSE:OXY), a key Berkshire Hathaway holding, has raised its dividend following strong sector performance and healthy cash flow. Berkshire Hathaway continues to hold a significant stake in Occidental, keeping investor focus on how this position fits within its wider portfolio approach. items.title: What ExxonMobil Told You Before The Oil Shock Arrived
items.summary: Two downstream start-ups and an early deepwater delivery were readable weeks ahead; the price that made them pay was not.

items.title: Occidental Petroleum Stock Can Climb Without A Higher Oil Price
items.summary: Management's own plan leans on lower costs, a slower decline rate, and a stronger balance sheet, not on the price of crude.
